newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi says unaware it broke US wheat trade rules.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi says unaware it broke US wheat trade rules.

text.p: Mitsubishi Corp said on Thursday it had been unaware it was breaking commodity futures trading rules in wheat futures trade it conducted on the Minneapolis Grain Exchange.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said on Wednesday that Mitsubishi Corp, along with Merrill Lynch Futures Inc and Country Hedging Inc settled charges of "wash trading" on wheat futures with the CFTC.
It said Mitsubishi agreed to pay $150,000.

"CFTC launched an investigation about four years ago on alleged suspicion that our buy and sell orders were regarded as 'wash trade', which is banned under U.S. commodity futures rules. At that time, we did not believe we were breaking the rules," a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
"But we have decided to accept the settlement, considering the high costs if we brought a lawsuit in the U.S.," the spokesman said.

CFTC said Mitsubishi tried to shift futures trading profits from one reporting period to another for accounting purposes by placing simultaneous orders with its brokerage firm, Merrill Lynch, to buy and sell equal quantities of wheat futures spreads at approximately the same price.
